groups.name: types-sample-and-views
groups.summary: Define shared TS types + sample fixture, then build GroupBoard/EventLog and wire into App.tsx.
groups.spec:
Implement T2 and T3 from the plan. This group builds on the `ui/` skeleton created by the scaffolding group (`ui/src/main.tsx`, `ui/src/App.tsx`, `ui/src/styles.css` already exist as placeholders) — you are filling in the real types, data, and view logic.

Part 1 — shared contracts and sample fixture (T2):
- `ui/src/types.ts`: define TypeScript types mirroring the orchestrator's models — a `GroupState` union type with exactly the values `"pending" | "ready" | "running" | "reviewing" | "rewriting" | "merging" | "completed" | "failed"`; a `GroupRunState` type with fields `state` (GroupState), `generation` (number), and `failure` (optional/nullable); a `RunState` type with `run_id` (string) and `groups: Record<string, GroupRunState>`; a `Manifest` shape with `run_id`, `base_session_id`, and `groups` mapping to sessions that each have `name`/`role`; and an `Escalation` shape with `id`, `kind`, `group_id`, `prompt`.
- `ui/src/sample-run.ts`: export a typed sample object (or objects) built from the `types.ts` contracts — a `RunState` with a handful of groups spanning different `GroupState` values, a matching `Manifest`, several event-log lines (strings, representing lines as they'd appear in `logs/run.log`), and at least one pending `Escalation`. This is the only data source for the UI in this version (no backend/network).

Part 2 — view components wired into App (T3):
- `ui/src/components/GroupBoard.tsx`: takes the `RunState` as a prop and renders one card per group, each showing the group id, its `generation`, and its `state`, with a visually distinct color per `GroupState` value (e.g. via a state→color mapping in the component or in `styles.css`).
- `ui/src/components/EventLog.tsx`: renders the event-log lines in order, and separately lists any pending escalations, each showing its `kind`, `group_id`, and `prompt`.
- `ui/src/App.tsx`: replace the scaffolded placeholder with a real composition — a header, then `GroupBoard`, then `EventLog` — passing in data from `ui/src/sample-run.ts`.

Constraints from the plan apply throughout: create source files only (no `npm install`/dev server/build — there is no network); keep the implementation small and readable; no router, no state management library; use plain CSS in `styles.css` for any additional styling needed by these components.

ui/src/sample-run.ts exports a typed sample using the types.ts contracts: a RunState with multiple groups across different states, a Manifest, several event-log lines, and at least one pending Escalation.

groups.name: scaffold-vite-project
groups.summary: Scaffold the Vite + React + TypeScript project skeleton under ui/ (config, entry, base styles).
groups.spec:
Implement T1 from the plan: scaffold the Vite + React + TypeScript project under `ui/`. This is the foundational group — create only the project skeleton, no view logic. Create these files under `ui/`: - `ui/package.json` — name/version fields are your choice; dependencies: `react`, `react-dom`; devDependencies: `vite`, `typescript`, `@vitejs/plugin-react`, `@types/react`, `@types/react-dom`; scripts: `"dev": "vite"` and `"build": "tsc && vite build"`. - `ui/tsconfig.json` — strict mode enabled, `"jsx": "react-jsx"`, `"target": "ES2020"`, and whatever module/moduleResolution/lib settings are needed for a Vite + React + TS project to type-check cleanly (e.g. `"module": "ESNext"`, `"moduleResolution": "bundler"`, DOM lib). - `ui/vite.config.ts` — uses `@vitejs/plugin-react`. - `ui/index.html` — contains a `
` and a ``. - `ui/src/main.tsx` — creates the React root on `#root` and renders `` wrapped in ``; imports `./styles.css`. - `ui/src/App.tsx` — a minimal placeholder component (this will be filled in by the group that builds the view components; keep it small, e.g. a functional component returning a simple wrapper element). - `ui/src/styles.css` — a clean, minimal base stylesheet (resets/typography/layout basics); imported from `main.tsx`.
